## Revenue forecasters' woes

- We don't truly know the present -- substantial data lags
- The past isn't what it used to be -- data revisions
- The economy we measure is not quite the economy we tax
- Must forecast *when* people pay, in addition to *what* they owe

Each issue adds to forecast risk.

::: notes
Lags - PIT data from tax returns -- 2023 is latest full file Data revisions -- employment data Economy we tax -- capital gains When people pay -- estimated tax and final returns
:::

## Population change since the 2020 Census

```{r}
#| label: pop-change-facets
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 10

keep <- c(
  "npopchg",
  "naturalchg",
  "domesticmig",
  "internationalmig"
)
labels <- c(
  "Net Population Change",
  "Natural Change (Births minus Deaths)",
  "Domestic Migration",
  "International Migration"
)

pop |>
  filter(variable %in% keep) |>
  filter(year > 2020) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = keep, labels = labels)) |>
  arrange(variable) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Net Population Change" = "steelblue",
      "Natural Change (Births minus Deaths)" = "seagreen",
      "Domestic Migration" = "coral",
      "International Migration" = "mediumpurple"
    )
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "change (thousands)",
    labels = scales::label_comma(scale = 1e-3, accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(-350e3, 350e3),
    breaks = seq(-400e3, 400e3, 100e3)
  ) +
  ggtitle("Annual Changes in New York State Population Since 2020 Census") +
  labs(
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau Population Estimates Program\nChanges are from July 1 to July 1"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 2, scales = "fixed") +
  theme_presentation() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.3), face = "bold")
  )

```

```{r}
#| label: employment-bench-nonbench-pchya

# compare NY Fed early benchmarked employment data to CES seasonally adjusted data

cesbase <- cesny |>
  filter(area_code == "00000", supersector_code == "00", seasonal == "S") |>
  arrange(date) |>
  mutate(src = "ces") |>
  select(date, src, value)

ebenchbase <- ebench |>
  filter(area == "ny") |>
  mutate(src = "ebench") |>
  select(date, src, value = emp)

pdata <- bind_rows(cesbase, ebenchbase) |>
  filter(year(date) >= 2000) |>
  arrange(date) |>
  mutate(pchya = value / lag(value, 12) - 1, .by = src)

```

```{r}
#| label: employment-bench-pchya-table
#| output: true

# for a table
pchya <- pdata |>
  mutate(year = year(date)) |>
  summarise(avgemp = mean(value), .by = c(year, src)) |>
  arrange(year, src) |>
  mutate(pchya = avgemp / lag(avgemp) - 1, .by = src)

data <- bind_rows(pchya, dobeea) |>
  filter(year >= 2019) |>
  select(year, src, pchya)

levs <- c("ces", "ebench", "dob")

labs <- c(
  ces = "Official employment (CES)",
  ebench = "Early benchmark (NY Fed)",
  dobeea = "Executive budget (DOB)"
)

data |>
  filter(year %in% 2023:2027) |>
  mutate(src = factor(src, levels = levs, labels = labs)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = pchya, names_prefix = "y") |>
  arrange(src) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    "NYS Employment History and Forecast",
    subtitle = "% Change vs. prior calendar year"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    src = "Source",
    y2023 = "2023",
    y2024 = "2024",
    y2025 = "2025",
    y2026 = "2026",
    y2027 = "2027"
  ) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = src) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = -src, decimals = 1) |>
  sub_missing(columns = -src, missing_text = "-") |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_fill(color = "#D9F2D9")),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = c(y2025, y2026, y2027),
      rows = src == "Executive budget (DOB)"
    )
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    "Sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CES), New York Federal Reserve Bank (NY Fed), and NYS Division of the Budget (DOB)"
  )

```

# Linking economic and tax-revenue forecasts

```{r}
#| label: get-agi-pi-data

# nysagi
# nyspi

agi2 <- nysagi |>
  filter(
    rstat == "All Filers",
    por == "All Places",
    county == "All Places",
    state == "All",
    country == "All"
  ) |>
  select(year, sortincome, agirange, numret:nyidadjust) |>
  arrange(sortincome, year)

agibase <- agi2 |>
  filter(sortincome == 16) |>
  select(year, nysagi) |>
  mutate(variable = "nysagi", value = nysagi) |>
  select(variable, year, value)

# agi2 |> filter(sortincome == 16) |> ggplot(aes(year, nysagi)) + geom_line()

pibase <- nyspi |>
  filter(linecode == 10, year %in% 2015:2023) |>
  mutate(
    variable = "nyspi",
    year = as.integer(year),
    value = as.numeric(value) * 1e6
  ) |>
  select(variable, year, value)

piagi <- bind_rows(pibase, agibase)

# piagi |> ggplot(aes(year, value, colour = variable)) + geom_line()
# piagi |>
#   pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value) |>
#   mutate(ratio = nyspi / nysagi) |>
#   ggplot(aes(year, ratio)) +
#   geom_line()
# pi is about 30-50% larger than agi depending on year

pdata <- piagi |>
  arrange(variable, year) |>
  mutate(pchya = value / lag(value) - 1, .by = variable) |>
  filter(year %in% 2016:2023)

```

## AGI vs. Personal Income Components

```{r}
#| label: get-agi-components

# nysagi
# nyspi
# wages, interest, dividends, capgains, caploss, rrpetgain, rrpetloss, busfarmgain, bus

agi_components <- nysagi |>
  filter(
    rstat == "All Filers",
    por == "All Places",
    county == "All Places",
    state == "All",
    country == "All"
  ) |>
  filter(sortincome == 16) |>
  select(
    year,
    numret,
    nysagi,
    wages,
    interest,
    dividends,
    capgains,
    caploss,
    rrpetgain,
    rrpetloss,
    busfarmgain,
    busfarmloss,
    pensions,
    otherinc
  ) |>
  arrange(year)

agibase <- agi_components |>
  mutate(
    intdiv = interest + dividends,
    capnet = capgains - caploss,
    rrpetnet = rrpetgain - rrpetloss,
    busfarmnet = busfarmgain - busfarmloss,
    allother = nysagi -
      wages -
      intdiv -
      capnet -
      rrpetnet -
      busfarmnet -
      pensions -
      otherinc
  ) |>
  select(
    year,
    nysagi,
    wages,
    intdiv,
    capnet,
    rrpetnet,
    busfarmnet,
    pensions,
    otherinc,
    allother
  ) |>
  arrange(year)

agibase2 <- agibase |>
  mutate(other = nysagi - wages - capnet) |>
  select(year, nysagi, wages, capnet, other)

# combine agi components plus nyspi
piagi <- agibase2 |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -year, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  bind_rows(pibase)

```

```{r}
#| label: show-pi-agi-components
#| output: false
#| eval: false
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 10

vars <- c("nyspi", "nysagi", "wages", "capnet")
var_labels <- c(

  )
```

# Wages and withholding

## Wages

```{r}
#| label: wage=prep

tmp <- count(qcew, naics_level, naics, naics_title)

wages <- qcew |>
  filter(areatype == "state") |>
  filter(naics == "00" | str_starts(naics, "523")) |>
  select(-c(areatype, area, estab, contains("emp")))

wages2 <- wages |>
  mutate(
    ind = case_when(
      naics == "00" ~ "total",
      naics == "523" ~ "finance",
      naics == "5231" ~ "securities",
      naics == "5232" ~ "exchanges",
      naics == "5239" ~ "other",
      .default = "ERROR"
    )
  ) |>
  select(date, ind, totwage) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = ind, values_from = totwage)

wages2 |>
  mutate(
    finshare = finance / total,
    across(c(finance, securities, exchanges, other), \(x) x / finance)
  )

wages3 <- wages2 |> select(date, total, finance)

```

```{r}
#| label: wages-plot
#| output: true

pdata <- wages3 |>
  rename(value = finance) |>
  filter(year(date) >= 2022) |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date) |> as.integer(),
    qtr = factor(
      paste0("Q", lubridate::quarter(date)),
      levels = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")
    )
  )

yr_min <- min(pdata$year)
yr_max <- max(pdata$year)

facet_means <- pdata |>
  summarise(mean_value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .by = qtr)

pdata |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(
    data = facet_means,
    aes(yintercept = mean_value),
    color = "red",
    linetype = "solid",
    linewidth = 0.5,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~qtr, nrow = 1, scales = "fixed") + # one row, same y-axis across months
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(yr_min, yr_max, by = 1),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.4)) # add internal left/right padding
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "", accuracy = 0.1),
    breaks = seq(0, 100e9, by = 10e9),
    # limits = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  theme_presentation() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.8)),
    plot.caption = ggtext::element_markdown(),
  ) +
  theme_rotate(angle = 90) +
  ggtitle(
    "QCEW Financial Sector (NAICS 523) Wages by Quarter, Calendar years 2023-2025",
    subtitle = "Red horizontal line is quarterly mean"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "$ billions",
    x = NULL,
    caption = "Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via NYS Department of Labor<br>**CAUTION: Vertical axis does not start at zero**"
  )

```

```{r}
  filter(vname == "pit_wh") |>
  filter(year(date) >= 2022) |>

  )

yr_min <- min(lubridate::year(pdata$date))

facet_means <- pdata |>

  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +

  ) +
  facet_wrap(~mon, nrow = 1, scales = "fixed") + # one row, same y-axis across months
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(yr_min, yr_max, by = 1),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.4)) # add internal left/right padding
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "", accuracy = 0.1),
    breaks = seq(0, 10e9, by = 500e6),
    # limits = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  theme_presentation() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.8)),
    plot.caption = ggtext::element_markdown(),
  ) +
  theme_rotate(angle = 90) +
  ggtitle(
    "PIT Withholding Tax Collections by Month, Calendar years 2022 through most recent",
    subtitle = "Red horizontal line is monthly mean"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "$ billions",
    x = NULL,
    # x = "Calendar year",
    caption = "Source: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance<br>**CAUTION: Vertical axis does not start at zero**"
  )
```

## Other states' recent revenue forecasts

```{r}
#| label: other-states-revenue-forecasts
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 9

# Create the data
revenue_growth <- tibble(
  fiscal_year = rep(
    c("FY 2024", "FY 2025", "FY 2026\nforecast", "FY 2027\nforecast"),
    each = 2
  ),
  tax_type = rep(c("Personal income tax", "Sales tax"), 4),
  value = c(
    0.3,
    1.1, # FY 2024
    7.3,
    2.5, # FY 2025
    3.8,
    3.2, # FY 2026
    2.6,
    2.9
  ) # FY 2027
) |>
  mutate(
    fiscal_year = factor(
      fiscal_year,
      levels = c("FY 2024", "FY 2025", "FY 2026\nforecast", "FY 2027\nforecast")
    ),
    tax_type = factor(tax_type, levels = c("Personal income tax", "Sales tax"))
  )

# Create the plot
revenue_growth |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fiscal_year, y = value, fill = tax_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(value, "%")),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Personal income tax" = "steelblue", "Sales tax" = "coral")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = NULL,
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1, accuracy = 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 8, 1),
    limits = c(0, 8.5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = NULL) +
  labs(
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center\nNote: 46 states have a July 1 fiscal year"
  ) +
  # annotate(
  #   "text",
  #   x = 1,
  #   y = 0.2,
  #   label = "Note: Most states have a July 1 fiscal year",
  #   hjust = 0,
  #   size = 3,
  #   color = "gray40"
  # ) +
  ggtitle(
    "State history and forecasted growth in personal income and sales tax",
    subtitle = "Median of 40 reporting states"
  ) +
  theme_presentation() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    # plot.caption = element_text(size = 10) # hjust = 0,
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = c(0.85, 0.85),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80"),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.5, "lines")
    # legend.text = element_text(size = 11) # ,
  )

```

## Capital gains episodes (national)

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
|  |  |  |
|----------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
| **Period** | **Capital gains realizations...** | **Context** |
| 1996-2000 | **rose** from 3.2% of GDP to 6.3% (+97%) | dot-com bubble, stock market boom |
| 2000-2003 | **fell** to 2.5% of GDP (-60%) | dot-com and stock market bust |
| 2003-2007 | **rose** to 6.4% of GDP (+156%) | housing bubble, bull stock market |
| 2007-2009 | **fell** to 1.8% of GDP (-72%) | Global Financial Crisis |
| 2009-2021 | **rose** to 8.7% of GDP (+383%) | Long slow recovery and COVID selloff |
| 2021-2023 | **fell** to 3.5% of GDP (-60%) | COVID shutdown and slow recovery |
| 2023-2025 | **rose** to 5.3% of GDP (+51%) (*estimated*) | strong stock market, NVIDIA, AI |

```{r}
#| label: experimental-employment
#| eval: false

qcew
ces
ebench

qcew2 <- qcew |>
  filter(areatype == "state", naics == "00", ownerf == 1) |>
  select(qdate = date, starts_with("mnth")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -qdate) |>
  mutate(monthadd = str_sub(name, 5, 5) |> as.integer() - 1) |>
  mutate(date = qdate + months(monthadd), src = "qcew") |>
  select(date, src, value)

ces2 <- ces |>
  filter(
    state_code == "36",
    area_code == "00000",
    supersector_code == "00",
    data_type_code == "01"
  ) |>
  mutate(src = ifelse(seasonal == "U", "ces_ns", "ces_s")) |>
  select(date, src, value)

ebench2 <- ebench |>
  filter(area == "ny") |>
  mutate(src = "ebench") |>
  select(date, src, value = emp)


skimr::skim_without_charts(ces2)

qcew2 |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point()

comp <- bind_rows(qcew2, ces2, ebench2) |>
  filter(year(date) >= 2000)

comp |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = src)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point()

wide <- comp |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = src, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(diff = ces_ns - qcew, pdiff = diff / qcew)

wide |>
  ggplot(aes(date, diff)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point()

wide |>
  ggplot(aes(date, pdiff)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point()

# library(feasts)
# library(tsibble)

# Convert to tsibble (time series tibble) with monthly interval
wide_ts <- wide |>
  filter(!is.na(pdiff)) |>
  mutate(month = yearmonth(date)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = month)

# Check for gaps (should be none now)
scan_gaps(wide_ts)

scan_gaps(wide_ts)

wide_ts |>
  filter(year(date) >= 2021) |>
  ggtime::gg_season(pdiff, period = "year") +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal Pattern of QCEW vs CES Employment Difference",

  )

comp |>
```
